lines: I have chased enough trouble from the flock to know when trouble has teeth.
I know the sound of everyone trying to get through one gate at once. I made it through.
I counted my steps back like I count heads at dusk.
A scattered mind is hard to gather. I managed it enough to get home.
The village gate felt like a pen after a long, bad storm.
I made it back with my heart running ahead of me.
Keeping calm is easier when no one is shouting. I did my best anyway.
I reached home and only then remembered to breathe properly.
The first blow knocked me down. Getting up was the hard decision.
I hid under a ledge until the arrows stopped.
My shield broke before my nerve did.
I ran when staying would have killed me. I will not apologize for that.
A healer pulled two splinters from my arm this morning.
I followed the sound of the bell when I could not see the road.
The fighting scattered us. I found my way back alone.
I lost my pack and kept my life. That was a fair trade.
There was blood on my sleeve that did not belong to me.
I still jump when someone drops a tool behind me.
I remember the quiet after more clearly than the noise.
I survived. I am not ready to make a brave story out of it.
